recentItems.title: How to belong without losing yourself | Reut Schwartz-Hebron | TEDxManitou Springs Salon
recentItems.description:
Why belonging feels risky, and five brave choices that shift it from something you hope others grant into a practice you cultivate. Reut Schwartz-Hebron is the founder of KCI (Key Change Institute) and a neuroscience-obsessed expert in human change, focused on transformation where it actually happens: inside the brain. For more than two decades, she has trained and certified hundreds of executive and life coaches in Advanced Applied Neuroscience, so they can support their coaching clients tackle one enduring human puzzle: why we struggle to adopt the changes we genuinely want. 

Beyond working with experienced coaches, Reut has coached brains and the people who belong to them across a wide range of settings, from elite military teams to Fortune 500 companies including Comcast, Phillips, and GSK. She is known for translating complex neuroscience into practical tools, and has written books and numerous articles on unlearning and difficult change, illuminating what’s really going on in the brain when change gets “too hard” and how lasting transformation becomes possible. 

This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx

recentItems.title: Are we asking the wrong questions after a career setback? | Margaret Weniger | TEDxAtlanta
recentItems.description:
You worked hard. Followed the advice. Then your career took a turn you never planned. Margaret Weniger went looking for what she’d done wrong. Hundreds of interviews later, she began to question the question itself. Margaret Weniger is challenging one of our most persistent ideas about work: that a successful career follows a predictable path.

After 12 years climbing the technology sales ladder, Margaret began studying what happens when carefully made career plans collide with layoffs, changing priorities and unexpected turns. Her research with professionals revealed that career disruption was far less unusual than we’ve been taught to believe. Her own experience gave the question particular urgency: Behind a résumé that looked successful, Margaret had been fired and laid off multiple times. 

Today, Margaret is director of Startup Launch at Georgia Tech’s CREATE-X, where she helps founders navigate uncertainty and build companies. She is also the author of “Broken: Designing Careers in a Flawed and Outdated System.” This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx

recentItems.title: The Hidden Power of Women Sharing What They Know | Ronda Carnegie | TEDxAmazônia
recentItems.description:
What if some of the world's most powerful solutions are already here, held in the wisdom of women whose voices too often go unheard?

When Ronda Carnegie gathered a circle of women to share what they wished they'd known at 16 with her young daughter, she discovered something that would take her across continents: knowledge can change lives, but trust and connection are what allow it to change the world.

From India and Ethiopia to Uganda and Colombia, Ronda reveals what becomes possible when women share what they know — and why the future may depend less on finding new answers than on recognizing the wisdom already among us. Ronda Carnegie is the Co-Founder and Executive Director of Project Dandelion, a global, women-led initiative that mobilizes collective leadership for a climate-safe, livable world. As a member of TED's leadership team, she helped transform TED from a conference into a global platform for ideas by building global partnerships, co-founding TEDWomen, and creating the TED Institute to surface untapped ideas and voices within organizations. Her career has spanned media, business, and social innovation, including leadership roles at The New Yorker and The Female Quotient. Across this work runs a common belief: transformative ideas and solutions already exist, and connection can help them change the world. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx

recentItems.title: Equality Isn't a Policy. It's a Practice We Teach at Home. | Christina Joymon | TEDxABQ
recentItems.description: Christina Joymon reframes gender equality in the workplace, asking if the real answer starts closer to home than we think. Christina Elizabeth Joymon is an engineer, investor, award-winning author, and global speaker bridging technology, entrepreneurship, leadership, and the arts. As Founder and General Partner of XIA Capital, she has spent over a decade investing in AI, sustainability, and women-led ventures, while advocating for women in STEM through ASME's Women's Leadership Collective and Project Aspire. She's also the award-winning novelist behind Royal Planet. Sparked by a defining classroom moment as a female engineering student, Christina's talk asks what it will really take to move the needle on gender equality — and why the answer may start closer to home than we think. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx

recentItems.title: Quantum Wellness: The Better Use for AI in Healthcare | Dr. Sageline LaBaze | TEDxABQ
recentItems.description: Dr. Sahgee reframes the future of medicine, asking what happens when AI catches illness months before diagnosis. Dr. Sageline LaBaze, known as Dr. Sahgee, is a first-generation Haitian American physician, a Preventive Medicine and Public Health resident at the University of New Mexico, and an MPH candidate at Johns Hopkins. Founder of Solterix Inc. and Solterica AI, she merges artificial intelligence with preventive health to dismantle systemic barriers before they become diagnoses. Her talk poses a striking question: what if your doctor knew you were getting sick months before you did? Drawing on her clinical experience and New Mexico's unique healthcare challenges, Dr. Sahgee explores where AI in medicine is headed next — and why it matters for all of us. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx

recentItems.title: The Overlooked Kid Who Became the Role Model She Needed | Anastasia Zagrai | TEDxABQ
recentItems.description: Anastasia Zagrai reframes who's equipped to inspire future scientists, asking if it's not the experts we'd expect at all. Anastasia Zagrai is a recent graduate of Socorro High School in rural New Mexico and an incoming civil engineering student at MIT. As an engineering researcher, Science Olympiad competitor, and founder of Socorro Sparks, she creates hands-on STEM experiences for local students. Anastasia believes students are often held back not by lack of interest, but by fear of being wrong. Drawing on her experience teaching rural youth through Socorro Sparks, her talk asks a provocative question: what if the people best equipped to inspire the next generation of scientists and engineers aren't who we expect at all? This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx

recentItems.title: Rethinking teenage stress | Miranda Garcia | TEDxABQ
recentItems.description: Miranda Garcia reframes teen stress, drawing on her own research to ask what we're getting wrong about supporting teenagers. Miranda Garcia is a senior at V. Sue Cleveland High School in Rio Rancho, New Mexico, whose STEM journey has taken her through Girls Who Code, Young Women in Computing, STEM Mavericks, and Higher Orbits' Go For Launch. She has engineered a seizure detection and alert system using a Raspberry Pi and conducted award-winning research on how breathing techniques affect stressed teenagers, alongside teaching STEM as an Education and Outreach Intern at R4 Creating. This fall she heads to New Mexico State University to study Chemical and Materials Engineering. In her talk, Miranda draws on her own research to ask what we might be getting wrong about how we support teenagers today. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx

recentItems.title: We Have to Work Together to Prevent Sexual Violence  | Mary Beth Lindsey | TEDxABQ
recentItems.description: Mary Beth Lindsey reframes sexual assault as everyone's public health crisis, not just the demographic left to fix it. Mary Beth Lindsey is an actor, singer, performer, and community advocate serving as Education & Prevention Manager for Solace Sexual Assault Services in Santa Fe, where she's also a well-known local emcee performing as Miss Anita Whiskey. In her talk, Mary Beth points to a striking disconnect: the professionals leading sexual assault recovery work are rarely the demographic most often responsible for perpetrating it. Drawing on CDC research, she makes the case for a different, more coordinated response to what she argues is a public health crisis touching all of us. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx

recentItems.title: You Don't Need to Dive to Discover | Samantha Schwann | TEDxABQ
recentItems.description: Samantha Schwann reframes exploration itself, showing how advancing ROV tech is expanding what the ocean can teach us. Samantha Schwann is an underwater visual artist and explorer working at the intersection of exploration, technology, and conservation. A member of The Explorer's Club, she pilots a remotely operated vehicle (ROV) to document biodiversity in the ocean's low-light “twilight zone,” where only a fraction of sunlight reaches. In her talk, Samantha shares findings from seven progressively challenging ROV expeditions into a submarine canyon, revealing hidden biodiversity and surprising marine events in an otherwise well-documented protected environment. As ROV technology advances, she shows how our understanding of the ocean's least-observed places is only beginning to unfold. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx

recentItems.title: Performance isn't Projection. It's Connection. | Elizabeth Garland | TEDxABQ
recentItems.description: From stage fright to Vienna's stages, Elizabeth Garland reframes confidence for introverts with what she calls Superpresence. Elizabeth Garland is an international composer, performer, educator, and performance coach who has performed at the World Composers Concert in Vienna, served as artist-in-residence at the Santa Fe Art Institute, and won honors including First Prize in the Unsigned Only Instrumental Competition. Her writing appears in the bestselling Power of Why series. Drawing on her own journey from stage fright to Vienna's concert halls, Elizabeth's talk challenges what sensitive, introverted performers are typically told about confidence — and introduces a different way forward she calls Superpresence. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx

recentItems.title: Confessions of a Serial Failure | Eddie Tafoya | TEDxABQ
recentItems.description: Eddie Tafoya reframes a lifetime of falling short of perfection, making the case that our flaws are exactly what the world needs. Eddie Tafoya is an Albuquerque native, English professor, author, and comedian featured in A&E's docuseries The Right to Offend: A Look at African American Comedy. His books include The Legacy of the Wisecrack, Icons of African American Comedy, and the novel Finding the Buddha, with The Marxist Revolution: How Chico, Harpo, Groucho, and Zeppo Changed the Way We Laugh releasing in 2027. In his talk, Eddie takes on a lifetime of messages about falling short of perfection — and makes an unexpected case for why our flaws might be exactly what the world needs from us. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx

recentItems.title: Crazy in Love | Jaime Campbell | TEDxABQ
recentItems.description: Jaime Campbell reframes what it takes to see someone as a whole person, drawn from her own story of diagnosis and love. Jaime Campbell is a Certified Peer Support Worker and disability advocate who began volunteering with children with disabilities at age 12, learning ASL along the way. At 19, she began her own journey with schizophrenia. After marrying her husband Jon, who lived with autism and psychosis and passed away due to gaps in specialized care, Jaime committed herself to bridging the mental illness and developmental disability communities. She's now completing her MSW. Her talk walks through her own story of diagnosis and love, and asks what it really takes to see someone as a whole person. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx
